messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
messages.body_plain:
> So in order to import a RIL population file in mm format (preliminary map built with onemap), could i import it as "backcross" and then change the cross description or is there no way to load such data in mm format?

Either the file needs to be changed, or the code that produced it, or R/qtl.

I've changed R/qtl to handle such files (I think): https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/commit/d45c3866f
If you install the devtools package (and if you have the necessary tools, including a fortran compiler, for compiling source packages) you can install the revised version of R/qtl from GitHub:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("kbroman/qtl@devel")

> I am currently comparing ordering with different settings in rqtl and onemap. It looks like some of the maps actually get worse when increasing numbers of iterations and window-size.
> Is it because it is stuck in an local optimum?
>
> Could you maybe give me some tips about optimising the orderMarkers() run? Or is it best to do this manually with some ripple() runs?

I'd want to use a *much* larger value for window(), though it'd take a very long time with that density of markers.

The map construction tools in R/qtl are not very automated and not well suited for very large numbers of markers.

>From the result that you're getting, it seems like the map needs to be folder over onto itself, at the center.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
messages.body_plain:
It shouldn't affect marker ordering, but only estimates of inter-marker distances.

When reading the data with read.cross, use the argument crosstype="riself".
Alternatively, after reading in the data, use convert2riself():

  mycross <- convert2riself(mycross)

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.38-4
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.38-4) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org) and will be on CRAN shortly.

See http://www.rqtl.org/STATUS.txt for a list of changes.  There major
changes are the following:

  Fixed a bug in scanone() when using weights with multiple phenotypes
  when some of the phenotypes contain missing values.

  Got rid of everything to do with degrees of freedom in scanone and
  scantwo. The checks seemed to offer little value but rather produced
  cryptic warnings that confused many users.

As always, I'd appreciate hearing any suggestions or comments or
complaints.

Karl Broman

messages.subject: Rqtl
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I recently encountered some strange issues with QTL mapping. I have a dataset with lots of 0 and few data points that are above 0. I first tried using the default model="normal", and I got several QTLs and everything seems to work fine. When I started adding more QTL via addqtl, I found another significant QTL that is only 0.7cM away from a QTL found at the beginning. The 1.5 LOD intervals of these two QTL overlap as well. What are the possible reasons for seeing such QTLs?

Also, I looked up QTL mapping for non-normal traits, and I first tried it with model="np". However, I stumbled in the fitqtl part as it only takes in model="normal" or "binary". Should I just try converting my data into 0s and 1s, and do everything with model="binary" instead? Do I lose power for doing it the binary way?

Thanks,
CJ

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Rqtl
messages.body_plain:
Artifacts of tightly-linked QTL are a constant problem; I don't have a good solution other than to not trust the case of QTL with <2 typed markers between them, and to delete them "manually".

For phenotypes with many 0's, I generally prefer to use an approach similar to that described in Broman (2003) Genetics 163:1169-1175, http://www.genetics.org/content/163/3/1169.long

Define two derived phenotypes: a binary trait the indicates ==0 or >0, and a quantitative trait where all of the individuals with 0 phenotype are treated as missing values.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Rqtl
messages.body_plain:
The multiple QTL analysis with fitqtl/addqtl should work with the binary model, but 2part and nonparametric are not implemented.

There's not really a multiple-QTL analogue for the single-QTL nonparametric analysis. But sometimes I convert phenotypes to normal quantiles and then apply the usual "normal" model. R/qtl includes a function nqrank() for this transformation. It's not ideal for the case of many ties at 0.

What issues did you encounter?

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Rqtl
messages.body_plain:
In fitting a model with a binary trait, the analysis method involves an iterative algorithm.

In most cases, you can ignore these "didn't converge" warnings. They often happen in regions with little evidence for a QTL.

Or you could increase the maxit argument (for the maximum number of iterations), or increase the tol argument (for the tolerance for convergence).

karl

Michel

In a backcross, having two crossovers right next to each other is highly unlikely due to crossover interference.
But in an intercross the two crossovers may have occurred on opposite chromosomes, and so would not be barred by crossover interference.
